veranderings.voor: gee jy dieselfde dinge vir jou eie kinders aan
veranderings.na: gee jy dieselfde dinge aan jou eie kinders oor
veranderings.rede: Customs are passed on with 'oorgee aan'; 'vir iemand aangee' means handing over an object.

veranderings.voor: en nog baie ander tale daarby
veranderings.na: en daarby nog baie ander tale
veranderings.rede: Placing 'daarby' before the noun phrase reads more naturally.
No list was given, only a number of languages, so 'lys' has no clear referent.
AWS: a comma separates the verb closing the relative clause from the main-clause verb that follows it.

veranderings.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
veranderings.voor: in 'n groot stad en 'n ander gesin
veranderings.na: in 'n groot stad, en 'n ander gesin
veranderings.rede: AWS 2017: 'en' joins two clauses that each have their own subject and verb, so a comma goes before it.

veranderings.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
veranderings.voor: Albei daardie gesinne behoort nog altyd
veranderings.rede: 'Nog altyd' means 'all along'; the sense here is 'still', which is 'steeds', and 'daardie' is redundant after 'albei'.

veranderings.blok: Kultuur sê nie hoe jy moet leef nie
veranderings.voor: Dit sit ook in die gewone dinge
veranderings.na: Dit lê ook in die gewone dinge
veranderings.rede: 'Iets lê in' is the usual idiom for where a quality is found.
The standard adjective form is 'Kaaps-Maleis(e)', and a dish comes 'uit' a cuisine.

veranderings.voor: in baie huise oor die land gebak
veranderings.na: in baie huise regoor die land gebak
veranderings.rede: 'Regoor die land' is the idiomatic phrase for 'across the country'.

veranderings.na: eerder as by sommer enige dag
veranderings.rede: 'Sommer enige dag' carries the intended 'just any day'; 'enige dag' alone reads oddly after 'bepaalde dag'.
'Gesterf het' is gentler and more usual when speaking of a family's bereavement.
'Daar sit' is colloquial for existence; 'daar is' is the natural form here.
'n Kwart' dangles without saying a quarter of what.
'Meer' on its own is unclear; 'meer as een' states the plural plainly.

vlae.rede: The study block says people in Durban 'gewoonlik' order a quarter, the glossary says 'dikwels'; the qualifiers differ and only the writer can say which is intended.
